objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026): under the parity law, can a growth rule that reads only bond distances between the current distinctions (no names, no history) settle its own dimension when the number of fresh distinctions per join is not handed to it? CUBIC-FROM-A-KNOT's joining policy is kept (extended to groups of any size, and with its cap of three as a control); the fresh count of every new junction is left to a count rule. First discriminators: which single count keeps the policy running from one knot; what the fewest counts that keep it running build; what random counts do; whether the stall at four picks a number. Serves G2 and G1; tests A97; related to A101 (the betweenness line's two). Stop: proofs, one frozen census, referee hand-off, report.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; refereed R1, confirmed with fixes, no Block; headline scoped): under the complete-round joining rule (A104) none of the count rules tested settles its dimension by itself; for count rules in general the grown pattern is the down-closed sets of the descent order of its one-parent junctions (Birkhoff), so a count rule only places offshoots; one count for every join must equal a lone first knot's size (in general the start's open distinctions), else a stall at round 2, 4 or 3, giving the a-fold counting pattern with bond balls r^a; the stall at four is the cap of three; the fewest counts close one knot into the 2^a pattern and conserve the chains they are handed; blind counts all stall by round 14; distance-only reading proved for the uniform count. 3,982-case census, 10 of 10 held.
stop_rule: Proofs, one frozen census, referee hand-off, report.
title: Can a growth rule read its own dimension from distances?
